LAWS AND REGULATIONS RELATING TO INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
Patent
Pursuant to the Patent Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國專利法》), which was most
recently amended by the NPCSC on October 17, 2020, and came into effect on June 1, 2021,
the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law of the PRC《( 中華人民共和國專利法實施
細則》), which was most recently amended by the State Council on December 11, 2023, and
came into effect on January 20, 2024, and the Measures for the Recordal of Patent
Licensing Contracts 《( 專利實施許可合同備案辦法》), promulgated by the China National
Intellectual Property Administration on June 27, 2011, and effective as of August 1, 2011,
invention means inventions, utility models, and designs. Invention means any new technical
solution proposed for a product, a process, or an improvement thereof. Utility model means
any new technical solution proposed for the shape, structure, or combination thereof of a
product, which is fit for practical use. Design means any new design of the shape, pattern,
or a combination thereof, or the combination of color with shape or pattern, of the whole or
a part of a product, which creates an esthetic feeling and is fit for industrial application.
The duration of patent rights for inventions is 20 years, for utility models is 10 years, and
for designs is 15 years, all counted from the date of filing.
Pursuant to the relevant provisions of the Patent Law of the PRC and its implementing
regulations, an invention made by a person in execution of the tasks of the entity to which
he belongs, or primarily by using the material and technical conditions of the entity, shall be
deemed a service invention. The right to apply for a patent for a service invention shall vest
in the entity. After the application is approved, the entity shall be the patentee. The entity
may dispose of the right to apply for a patent for a service invention-creation and the patent
rights thereof in accordance with the law, so as to promote the implementation and
application of the relevant invention. The entity that is granted the patent right shall reward
the inventor or designer of the service invention. After the invention-creation patent is
implemented, the inventor or designer shall be given a reasonable remuneration based on
the scope of its application and the economic benefits obtained. The State encourages
entities granted patent rights to implement property rights incentives, adopting methods
such as equity, options, and dividends, to enable inventors or designers to reasonably share
in the benefits of innovation.
Trademark
Pursuant to the Trademark Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國商標法》), which was
most recently amended by the NPCSC on April 23, 2019, and came into effect on November

和國商標法實施條例》)which was amended on April 29, 2014, and came into effect on May
1, 2014, the term of validity of a registered trademark is ten years, calculated from the date
of its approval and registration. If there is a need to continue using the registered trademark
upon the expiration of its term of validity, the registration renewal procedures must be
completed in accordance with the relevant regulations within 12 months prior to the
expiration date. If the procedures cannot be completed within this period, a six-month grace
extension may be granted. Each renewal of a registered trademark is valid for ten years,

Copyright
Pursuant to the Copyright Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國著作權法》), which was
most recently amended by the NPCSC on November 11, 2020, and came into effect on June

organizations, that is, intellectual achievements in the fields of literature, art, and science
that are original and can be expressed in a certain form, shall enjoy copyright in accordance
with the law, regardless of whether they are published. Copyright includes a series of
personal rights and property rights such as the right of publication, the right of attribution,
the right of revision, the right to protect the integrity of the work, and the right of
reproduction.
Pursuant to the Regulations on the Security Protection of Computer Information

of computer information systems shall ensure the security of computers and their related
and supporting equipment and facilities, including networks, the security of the operating
environment, the security of information, and the normal functioning of computer
functions, so as to maintain the secure operation of computer information systems.

LAWS AND REGULATIONS RELATING TO ANTI-MONOPOLY AND ANTI-UNFAIR
COMPETITION
Anti-Monopoly Law
Pursuant to the Anti-Monopoly Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國反壟斷法》)(the
‘‘Anti-Monopoly Law’’), which was promulgated by the Standing Committee of the National
People’s Congress on August 30, 2007, effective from August 1, 2008, and subsequently
amended on June 24, 2022, effective from August 1, 2022, the Anti-Monopoly Law applies
to monopolistic conducts in economic activities within the territory of China, as well as
monopolistic conducts outside China that have the effect of eliminating or restricting
competition in the domestic market. The monopolistic conducts stipulated in the
Anti-Monopoly Law include undertakings reaching monopoly agreements, undertakings
abusing their dominant market position, and concentrations of undertakings that have or
may have the effect of eliminating or restricting market competition. The anti-monopoly
enforcement authority of the State Council is responsible for anti-monopoly enforcement
work in accordance with the provisions of the Anti-Monopoly Law. The anti-monopoly
enforcement authority of the State Council may, based on work requirements, authorize the
relevant authorities of the provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under
the central government to be responsible for the relevant anti-monopoly enforcement work.
Where an undertaking violates the provisions of the Anti-Monopoly Law, the
anti-monopoly enforcement authority shall order the cessation of the illegal conduct and
may impose a fine.
Anti-Unfair Competition Law
Pursuant to the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, which was promulgated by the NPCSC
on September 2, 1993, became effective on December 1, 1993, and was most recently
amended on June 27, 2025 and effective as of October 15, 2025, undertakings shall adhere to
the principles of voluntariness, equality, fairness, and good faith in their market
transactions, and shall comply with law and business ethics. The term ‘‘unfair

LAWS AND REGULATIONS RELATING TO CYBERSECURITY, DATA SECURITY,
AND PRIVACY PROTECTION
Cybersecurity and Data Security
The Ministry of Public Security of the PRC promulgated the Administration Measures
on the Security Protection for International Connections to Computer Information
Networks 《( 計算機信息網絡國際聯網安全保護管理辦法》) on December 16, 1997, which
was amended by the State Council of the PRC on January 8, 2011. As indicated in the
measures, no individual shall use the internet to endanger state security, divulge state
secrets, infringe on legitimate rights and interests of others or engage in criminal activities.
If an internet information service provider violates these measures, the Ministry of Public
Security and the local security public bureaus may issue a warning, confiscate its illegal
gains or impose a fine, terminate its network connection and, in severe cases, revoke its
operating license and shut down its websites.
Internet information in China is regulated and restricted from a national security
standpoint. The NPCSC enacted the Decisions on Maintaining Internet Security《( 全國人民
代表大會常務委員會關於維護互聯網安全的決定》) on December 28, 2000 and amended it on
August 27, 2009, which may subject violators to criminal punishment in China if such act
constitutes a criminal offense for any effort to: (i) hacking into a computer information
system relating to state affairs, national defense or cutting-edge science and technology; (ii)
intentionally creating and spreading destructive programs such as computer viruses to
attack computer systems and communications networks, thus damaging computer systems
and the communications networks; (iii) in violation of national regulations, discontinuing
computer networks or communications services without authorization, as a result of which
the computer network or communication system cannot function normally; (iv) leaking
state secrets; (v) spreading false information for commodities or services; (vi) infringing
intellectual property rights through the internet; or (vii) other illegal activities prescribed in
the Decisions on Maintaining Internet Security.
The Provisions on Technological Measures for Internet Security Protection《( 互聯網安
全保護技術措施規定》), which were promulgated on December 13, 2005 by the Ministry of
Public Security and came into effect on March 1, 2006, require internet service providers
and organizations that use internet services to implement technical measures for internet
security protection, including technical measures for preventing any incident or act that
may endanger network security, for example, computer viruses, network intrusions or
attacks to or destruction of the network. All internet access service providers are required to
take measures to keep a record of and preserve user registration information. Under these

According to the PRC National Security Law《( 中華人民共和國國家安全法》) enacted
by the NPCSC on February 22, 1993 and latest revised on July 1, 2015, the state shall
establish systems and mechanisms for national security review and supervision, conduct
national security review on key technology, network information technology products and
services related to state security to prevent and mitigate state security risks in an effective
way.
Furthermore, the Cybersecurity Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國網絡安全法》) was
promulgated on November 7, 2016 which took effect on June 1, 2017, most recently
amended on October 28, 2025 and effective as of January 1, 2026. Pursuant to this law, no
individual or organization may steal or obtain personal information through other illegal
means, or illegally sell or illegally provide personal information to others. Those who
construct or operate networks or provide services through networks shall, in accordance
with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations and the mandatory requirements
under national standards, take technical and other necessary measures to ensure
cybersecurity and stable operation, effectively respond to cybersecurity incidents, prevent
cyber-related illegal and criminal activities, and maintain the integrity, confidentiality and
availability of network data. In the event of a violation of the relevant provisions and
requirements under the Cybersecurity Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國網絡安全法》),
individuals or organizations may face penalties including warnings, fines, confiscation of
illegal gains, revocation of licenses, or closure of websites, and may be subject to criminal
liability in serious circumstances.
Pursuant to the Data Security Law of the PRC《( 中華人民共和國數據安全法》), which
was promulgated by the NPCSC on June 10, 2021, and came into effect on September 1,
2021, entities carrying out data processing activities shall comply with laws and
administrative regulations, respect social morality and ethics, adhere to business and
professional ethics, act in good faith, fulfill data security protection obligations, assume
social responsibility, and shall not endanger national security or public interests, nor harm
the lawful rights and interests of individuals or organizations. Any organization or
individual collecting data shall employ lawful and proper means and shall not acquire data
through theft or other illegal methods.
The Network Data Security Management Regulations《( 網絡數據安全管理條例》) were
promulgated by the State Council on September 24, 2024, and will take effect on January 1,
2025. Operating within the existing data protection framework established by the
Cybersecurity Law of the PRC, the Data Security Law of the PRC, and the Personal
Information Protection Law of the PRC, the Network Data Security Management
Regulations provide detailed implementation rules and guidance on various aspects of
data compliance requirements. This regulation applies to network data processing activities
and their security supervision within the PRC territory, with key provisions including: (i)
clarifying requirements for formulating and declaring important data catalogues; (ii)
optimizing cross-border data management by distinguishing obligations between the critical

Cybersecurity Review and Outbound Data Transfer Security Assessment
The Cybersecurity Review Measures 《( 網絡安全審查辦法》) were promulgated on
December 28, 2021, and took effect on February 15, 2022. These Measures stipulate CIIOs
procuring network products and services, as well as online platform operators carrying out
data processing activities that do or may affect national security, shall undergo
cybersecurity review. The Cybersecurity Review Measures further stipulate a
cybersecurity review shall be conducted in the following circumstances: (i) internet
platform operators who possess more than one million users’ personal information and
seek to list abroad are obliged to apply for a cybersecurity review; (ii) CIIOs purchasing
network products or services where national security has been or may be affected shall
apply for a cybersecurity review; and (iii) the competent PRC government authority may
initiate cybersecurity review in case that any member of the cybersecurity review committee
believes that any network product or service or data processing activity affects or is likely to
affect national security and the Central Cyberspace Affairs Commission approves to do so.
On July 7, 2022, the CAC (the Cyberspace Administration of China) promulgated the
Measures on Security Assessment of Outbound Data Transfer 《( 數據出境安全評估辦法》),
which came into effect on September 1, 2022. Pursuant to the measures, data processors
providing data overseas shall apply for outbound data transfer security assessment with the
CAC in any of the following circumstances: (i) where a data processor provides important
data abroad; (ii) where a CIIO or a data processor processing the personal information of
more than one million individuals provides personal information abroad; (iii) where a data
processor has provided personal information of 100,000 individuals or sensitive personal
information of 10,000 individuals in total abroad since January 1 of the previous year; and
(iv) other circumstances prescribed by the CAC for which declaration for security
assessment for outbound data transfers is required.
On March 22, 2024, the CAC promulgated the Provisions on Promoting and

effective on the date of promulgation. According to the provisions, (i) where a data
processor other than CIIO transfers personal information (excluding sensitive personal
information) abroad of more than 100,000 but less than 1 million persons, or the sensitive
personal information of less than 10,000 persons cumulatively as of January 1 of the current
year, it shall enter into a standard contract for outbound transmission of personal
information with overseas recipients or passing a security certificate on the protection of
personal information according to the law； (ii) where a data processor transfers data
abroad, it may be exempted from applying for a cross-border transfer security assessment,
concluding a standard contract for personal information to be provided abroad or passing a
security certificate for protection of personal information if it satisfies any of the following
conditions: (a) where it is really necessary to provide personal information abroad for the

Pursuant to the Critical Information Infrastructure Security Protection Regulations
《( 關鍵信息基礎設施安全保護條例》) promulgated by the State Council on July 30, 2021, and
effective from September 1, 2021, critical information infrastructure refers to important
network facilities and information systems in key industries and fields such as public
communications, information services, energy, transportation, water conservancy, finance,
public services, e-government, and national defense science and technology industries, as
well as other critical network facilities and information systems that, if destroyed, rendered
dysfunctional, or subject to data breaches, may seriously endanger national security, the
national economy, and public interests. The department responsible for the security
protection of critical information infrastructure (the ‘‘protection authority’’) shall formulate
identification rules for critical information infrastructure, organize the identification of
such infrastructure within its respective industry or sector in accordance with such rules,
and promptly notify the relevant operators of the identification results. During the track
record period and up to the latest practicable date, we have not received any notification
from the protection authority regarding our company being identified as a critical
information infrastructure operator.

REGULATORY OVERVIEW
Regulations on Privacy Protection
On December 29, 2011, the MIIT issued Several Provisions on Regulating the Market
Order of Internet Information Services 《( 規範互聯網信息服務市場秩序若干規定》), which
became effective on March 15, 2012, and provides that an internet information service
provider may not collect any user’s personal information or provide any such information
to third parties without such user’s consent, unless otherwise provided by laws and
administrative regulations. Pursuant to the Several Provisions on Regulating the Market
Order of Internet Information Services, internet information service providers are required
to, among others, (i) expressly inform the users of the method, content and purpose of the
collection and processing of such users’ personal information and may only collect such
information necessary for the provision of its services; and (ii) properly maintain the users’
personal information, and in case of any leak or possible leak of a user’s personal
information, internet information service providers must take immediate remedial measures
and, in severe circumstances, make an immediate report to the telecommunications
regulatory authority and cooperate with relevant authorities in investigation and
resolution.
Pursuant to the Decision on Strengthening the Protection of Online Information《( 關
於加強網絡信息保護的決定》), issued by the NPCSC on December 28, 2012, and the
Provisions on the Protection of Telecommunication and Internet User’s Personal
Information 《( 電信和互聯網用戶個人信息保護規定》), issued by the MIIT on July 16,
2013 and effective on September 1, 2013, any collection and use of any user personal
information must be subject to the consent of the user, follow the principles of legality,
rationality, and necessity, and fall within the specified purposes, methods and scopes in the
applicable law.
In addition, the Cybersecurity Law of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國網絡安全法》)
provides that: (i) to collect and use personal information, network operators shall follow
the principles of legality, legitimacy and necessity, disclose rules of data collection and use,
clearly express the purposes, means and scope of collecting and using the information, and
obtain the consent of the persons whose data is collected; (ii) network operators shall
neither collect personal information unrelated to the services they provide, nor collect or
use personal information in violation of the provisions of laws and administrative
regulations or the scopes of consent given by the persons whose data is collected; and shall
dispose of personal information they have saved in accordance with the provisions of laws
and administrative regulations and agreements reached with users; and (iii) network
operators shall not divulge, tamper with or damage the personal information they have
collected, and shall not provide personal information to others without the consent of the
persons whose data is collected. However, there will be an exception to the rules if the
information has been processed and cannot be recovered, making it impossible to identify
specific individuals.
Pursuant to the Civil Code of the PRC 《( 中華人民共和國民法典》), which came into
effect on January 1, 2021, the personal information of natural persons is protected by law.
Any organization or individual shall, when necessary, obtain personal information of others

The Personal Information Protection Law of the PRC《( 中華人民共和國個人信息保護
法》) was promulgated by the NPCSC on August 20, 2021, and became effective on
November 1, 2021. In accordance with this Law, the processing of personal information
shall have a definite and reasonable purpose, be directly related to the processing purpose,
and be conducted in a manner that minimizes the impact on individuals’ rights and
interests. The collection of personal information shall be limited to the minimum scope
necessary to achieve the purpose of processing, and excessive collection of personal
information is prohibited. Personal information processors are responsible for the personal
information they process and shall take necessary measures to safeguard the security of the
processed personal information. No organization or individual may illegally collect, use,
process, transmit, sell, provide, or disclose the personal information of others, nor engage
in personal information processing activities that endanger national security or public
interests.
LAWS AND REGULATIONS RELATING TO SECURITIES AND BY DOMESTIC
COMPANIES
The Securities Law of the PRC, as most recently amended by the NPCSC on December
28, 2019, and effective from March 1, 2020, comprehensively governs activities in the
domestic securities market of China, including securities issuance and trading, the takeover
of listed companies, securities exchanges, and securities companies, as well as the
responsibilities of securities regulatory authorities. The Securities Law further stipulates
that domestic enterprises in China issuing securities overseas directly or indirectly, or
having their securities listed and traded overseas, shall comply with the relevant regulations
prescribed by the State Council. Specific measures for the subscription and trading of shares
of domestic companies in foreign currencies shall be separately stipulated by the CSRC,
established by the State Council, is the securities regulatory authority responsible for the
supervision and administration of the securities market in accordance with the law,
maintaining market order, and ensuring its lawful operation. Currently, the issuance and
trading of H-shares are primarily governed by the regulations and rules promulgated by the
State Council and the CSRC.
Pursuant to the Trial Measures for the Administration of Overseas Issuance and
Listing of Securities by Domestic Enterprises 《( 境內企業境外發行證券和上市管理試行辦
法》), promulgated by the CSRC on February 17, 2023, and effective from March 31, 2023, a
domestic enterprise conducting an initial public offering or listing overseas shall file a
record with the CSRC within three business days after submitting the application
documents for issuance and listing to the overseas regulatory authority.

HISTORY AND CORPORATE STRUCTURE
OVERVIEW
Our history can be traced back to December 1993, when Mr. Dong, our Chairman,
executive Director and general manager, Mr. Chen, our deputy Chairman and executive
Director, and Ms. Li Xia founded our Company under the name of Shanghai Siyuan
Electric Co. Ltd.* (上海思源電氣有限公司) in Shanghai, the PRC. After over three decades
of development and growth, we are now a global power transmission and distribution
equipment manufacturer and integrated power and energy solution provider.
In December 2000, our Company was converted into a joint stock company with
limited liability and was renamed as Shanghai Sieyuan Electric Co., Ltd. (上海思源電氣股份
有限公司). In August 2004, our Company was listed on the main board of the Shenzhen
Stock Exchange (stock code: 002028.SZ). In December 2006, our Company was renamed as
Sieyuan Electric Co., Ltd. (思源電氣股份有限公司).

HISTORY AND CORPORATE STRUCTURE
Following completion of several rounds of capital increases and share transfers
between September 1996 to December 2000, our registered capital was increased to RMB3
million by December 2000, of which Mr. Dong, our Chairman, executive Director and
general manager, directly held 29.16% equity interests in our Company, each of Mr. Chen
and Ms. Li Xia directly held 21.87% equity interests in our Company, and other eight
shareholders held the remaining 27.10% equity interests in our Company, none of which
individually owned 10.00% or more of the equity interests in our Company and all of them
are Independent Third Parties as of the Latest Practicable Date.
Conversion into a Joint Stock Company in December 2000
On December 30, 2000, our Company was converted into a joint stock company with a
registered capital of RMB36 million, comprising 36,000,000 shares with a par value of
RMB1.00 each, and was renamed as Shanghai Sieyuan Electric Co. Ltd.
Capital Increase in June 2003
Following the conversion, our Company further underwent a round of capital increase
by the then shareholders. In May 2003, our Company effected a distribution comprising a
cash distribution and distribution in specie by distributing shares in our Company to all the
then shareholders. This distribution was made on the basis of our Company’s 36,000,000
shares outstanding as at the end of 2002. Bonus shares were distributed to all shareholders
at a rate of one bonus share for every ten shares held, together with a cash dividend of
RMB0.25 (tax inclusive) for every ten shares held, resulting in the distribution of an
aggregate of 3,600,000 bonus shares and cash dividends totaling RMB900,000 (tax
inclusive). Our Company’s registered share capital was then increased to RMB39.6
million, with a total of 39,600,000 shares issued to all shareholders based on their respective
shareholdings.
Listing on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in August 2004
In August 2004, we completed the listing of our A Shares on the Shenzhen Stock
Exchange (stock code: 002028.SZ), pursuant to which we issued an aggregate of 13,400,000
A Shares, accounting for approximately 25.28% of our Company’s share capital
immediately following the A Share listing.
Capitalization of Capital Reserve in June 2005
Pursuant to resolutions passed by the board of directors in February 2005 and
resolutions passed by the shareholders in April 2005, our Company capitalized its capital
reserve into share capital on the basis of ten additional shares for every ten shares held.
Upon completion of the capitalization, our registered share capital increased to RMB106
million with the total issued share capital of our Company increased to 106,000,000 A
Shares.

MAJOR ACQUISITIONS, DISPOSALS AND MERGERS
During the Track Record Period, our Group had actively sought investment
opportunities which are in line with our business objectives through acquisitions. We
have carried out the following major acquisition:
Acquisition of GMCC Electronic Technology Wuxi
On December 28, 2022 and April 25, 2023, our Company entered into share transfer
agreements with certain shareholders of GMCC Electronic Technology Wuxi, all of whom
are Independent Third Parties to our Company. Pursuant to such agreements, our
Company acquired an aggregate of approximately 60.42% equity interest in GMCC
Electronic Technology Wuxi at an aggregate consideration of RMB906,268,500. The
consideration was determined on the basis of arm’s length negotiations between the parties
with reference to the overall valuation of GMCC Electronic Technology Wuxi of RMB1.5
billion.
GMCC Electronic Technology Wuxi was established in 2010 and is a national
high-tech enterprise engaged in the research and development, manufacturing and sales of
power-type energy storage devices, including supercapacitors. It is currently one of a small
number of enterprises that possess core technologies and key materials for supercapacitors
based on dry-process electrode manufacturing. By further increasing its equity interest in
GMCC Electronic Technology Wuxi through equity transfer arrangements, our Company
expects to better integrate the technological and market advantages of both parties,
promote the application of supercapacitors in relevant fields, develop our Company’s
secondary growth-driving business line and enhance its overall competitiveness.

BUSINESS
OVERVIEW
Who We Are
We are a global power transmission and distribution equipment manufacturer and
integrated power and energy solution provider. According to Frost & Sullivan, in terms of
revenue in the power transmission, distribution and control equipment market for 2024 in
China, we ranked eighth among international enterprises, fifth among domestic enterprises
and third among domestic non-state-owned enterprises, with a market share of 3.5%. As a
major non-state-owned player in China’s power equipment sector, we are committed to
long-term sustainable development and have been deeply engaged in the power and energy
solutions field for more than three decades. We focus on the R&D, design, production and
sales of power transmission and distribution equipment and their core components, and
provide related EPC and full lifecycle services.
As one of the few companies in the industry with capabilities across primary
equipment, secondary equipment and energy-storage-related equipment as well as
integrated solutions, we have built a business model covering six core business lines:
switchgear, transformers, protection and automation, power electronics, energy storage
systems and components and EPC, which together form a business ecosystem of ‘‘products
+ solutions + services’’ with a rich portfolio widely applied across power grids, new energy
(photovoltaic and wind), metallurgy, petrochemicals, transportation, data centers and other
diverse scenarios. The following chart shows our main business layout:

Our Industry Opportunities
The global transition in energy structure continues to progress, supported by the
increasing integration of renewable energy and the growing need to upgrade and retrofit
existing power grids. These factors collectively underpin the long-term growth
opportunities for the power transmission, distribution and control equipment industry.
Against the backdrop of major countries and regions around the world actively pursuing
decarbonization commitments, investment in key areas such as renewable energy
generation, flexible AC/DC transmission, intelligent substations and power quality
enhancement continues to expand, providing structural growth momentum to the power
equipment industry chain. Meanwhile, continued industrialization and infrastructure
development in emerging economies further reinforce the growth foundation of the
global power transmission and distribution equipment market. According to Frost &
Sullivan, the global power transmission, distribution and control equipment market grew
from RMB580.8 billion in 2020 to RMB863.6 billion in 2024, representing a CAGR of
10.4%. The market is expected to further expand to RMB1,475.5 billion by 2029, with a
projected CAGR of 11.3% from 2025 to 2029, reflecting sustained and robust industry
expansion.
Driven by these trends, we have developed a strong ability to capture industry
opportunities through our comprehensive industry chain layout covering primary
equipment, secondary equipment, power electronics, energy storage systems and
components and EPC services. Our products and services span power generation,
transmission, transformation, distribution, utilization and storage, enabling us to serve
high-growth areas such as new-type power system development, renewable energy grid
connection, ultra-high-voltage AC/DC transmission projects and large-scale energy storage
deployment. Throughout this process, market demand for our high-voltage switchgear,
transformers, protection and automation systems, grid-forming power electronics
technologies and system stability solutions has continued to rise, providing strong
momentum for our business growth.
In addition, customer demand worldwide is rapidly shifting from supplying
stand-alone products to offering integrated solutions. Leveraging our vertically integrated
R&D and production system, extensive engineering and project experience, as well as a
marketing and service network covering more than 100 countries and regions worldwide as

2024 by 32.9% to RMB13,827.0 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Our
net profit also increased from RMB1,608.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2023 by
29.6% to RMB2,084.8 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, and increased from
RMB1,519.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2024 by 49.5% to

and 2025, respectively. For the years ended December 31, 2023, 2024 and the nine months
ended September 30, 2025, our return on equity reached 15.9%, 18.0% and 21.8%.

BUSINESS
OUR COMPETITIVE STRENGTHS
A Leading Non-State-Owned Power Equipment Brand Built Through Thirty Years of Deep
Industry Engagement
Since our founding in 1993, we have been focusing on power transmission and
distribution industry, maintaining a disciplined professional approach while benefiting
from the broader development of the non-state-owned economy. In line with the emergence
of new power systems and global grid infrastructure, we have expanded our product
portfolio to include primary equipment, secondary equipment and energy storage systems,
which form key components of the power transmission and distribution system. With a
forward-looking view of industry developments, we continue to refine and enhance our
products and maintain competitive positions in key product categories.
We entered core power transmission and distribution equipment segment in 2002,
proactively laying out gas-insulated switchgear, power electronics and digital protection.
This enabled portfolio coverage across primary and secondary equipment and progressively
developed our overall business layout. We successfully developed a mechanical DC circuit
breaker and deployed it in a landmark DC project. Our self-developed 500 kV eco-friendly
gas-insulated current transformer has been successfully commercialized, and our
self-developed grid-forming supercapacitor-based static synchronous condenser
(E-STATCOM) has been commissioned at a substation located at an elevation of 4,300
meters, where it has demonstrated reliable performance under extreme environmental
conditions. According to Frost & Sullivan, in terms of revenue from disconnectors and
instrument transformers for 2024 in China, we ranked second among domestic enterprises
and first among domestic non-state-owned enterprises.
Our energy storage business aligns with the needs of new-type power systems and
renewable energy integration. We have launched high-rate, long-life supercapacitor energy
storage systems with charge/discharge rates above 100 C and lifecycles exceeding one
million cycles, suitable for frequency regulation applications. In 2024, we successfully
mass-produced grid-forming energy storage systems capable of independently supporting
grid voltage and frequency, helping to address stability issues at renewable energy plants
and reliability challenges at grid edges and for sensitive loads. We have also expanded into
the automotive electronics sector, including on-board auxiliary power and door-lock safety
devices, with products supplied to leading domestic and international OEMs.
Sustained R&D Investment and Technological Innovation Underpinning Leadership
We maintain strong investment in R&D, with a focus on sustained input into
forward-looking and fundamental research. For the years ended December 31, 2023, 2024
and the nine months ended September 30, 2025, our research and development expenses
were RMB916.8 million, RMB1,110.0 million and RMB944.7 million, respectively. Our
research and development expenses as a percentage of revenue remained at a relatively high
level compared with industry peers, supporting our ongoing innovation and product
development efforts. We have established a strong R&D team covering a broad range of
areas from high- to low-voltage and from primary to secondary equipment.
Cross-disciplinary collaboration within the team provides synergies and supports

advanced technologies.

BUSINESS
Integrated Solution Capabilities Enabled by Industry-Chain Synergies Allowing Us to Deliver
High-Efficiency, High-Quality Outcomes Worldwide
As one of the few players with R&D and production capabilities across core power
transmission and distribution equipment, we have built an industrial layout spanning six
core business lines, including switchgear, transformers, protection and automation, power
electronics, energy storage and components and EPC, forming an ecosystem of ‘‘products +
solutions + services’’. Leveraging synergies across our business lines, we are able to
independently supply core equipment, resulting in a high overall in-house production rate
for substation-related equipment. This ensures consistency and reliability in project
execution and enables us to deliver stable and efficient integrated solutions to our
customers.
Leveraging the core advantages created through our integrated industry-chain layout,
we have successfully advanced from supplying stand-alone products to offering full-lifecycle
integrated solutions. We are able to provide customers with comprehensive, one-stop
services covering preliminary technical consulting, customized solution design, core
equipment manufacturing, engineering and construction, installation and commissioning,
and long-term operation and maintenance support. In major national projects, including
ultra-high-voltage substation construction and renewable-energy power-plant grid
integration, we have significantly enhanced project delivery efficiency and system
reliability through deep collaboration across our business lines, thereby establishing a
strong differentiated competitive edge. This service model not only meets customers’
demand for product compatibility, system stability and service continuity, but also
effectively reduces their overall procurement and management costs, further strengthening
customer stickiness and reinforcing our competitive position in the industry.
We have accumulated extensive experience in EPC projects. Our delivery of overseas
500 kV ultra-high-voltage substation EPC projects has demonstrated our capability to
undertake complex, high-standard international power engineering works. In the renewable
energy segment, we possess core capabilities for rapid full-substation commissioning and
delivery, significantly shortening project timelines. We also provide station-level
energy-storage EPC solutions. Leveraging our full industry-chain strengths in
independent R&D and manufacturing, together with efficient internal coordination, we
are able to independently supply and deeply integrate core equipment in EPC projects,
delivering highly customized, cost-controlled, and schedule-controlled one-stop services to
our customers.
Leading Global Footprint Driving Strong Overseas Growth
As of September 30, 2025, our business had covered more than 100 countries and
regions across six continents. In our overseas market expansion, we have successfully
entered the supply chains of Europe’s leading power grid operators, establishing long-term
and stable partnerships with renowned utilities in countries such as Italy and Belgium. We
have also achieved product breakthroughs in markets including the United Kingdom, Saudi
Arabia and Kuwait, and completed a strategic upgrade from equipment exports to
integrated exports of technology, standards and services.

The switchgear business is one of our core foundational businesses. Switchgear serves
as the ‘‘safety gate’’ of power systems, performing the core functions of circuit control,
protection and fault isolation. We have established a comprehensive product portfolio
covering high-, medium- and low-voltage switchgear, which is widely applied across power
generation, power transmission and distribution, as well as other application scenarios in
industrial, commercial and transportation sectors, thereby providing reliable and robust
safety assurance for power networks. According to Frost & Sullivan, in terms of revenue in
the switchgear market for 2024 in China, we ranked fourth among domestic enterprises and
third among domestic non-state-owned enterprises.
Switchgear, especially high-voltage gas-insulated switchgear, features high technical
barriers. In ultra-high-voltage gas-insulated switchgear, we achieved key breakthroughs and
domestic substitution. For example, our 750 kV gas-insulated switchgear has been delivered
to major power grid operators with internationally leading performance parameters, our

High-Voltage Gas-Insulated Switchgear
High-voltage gas-insulated switchgear is a type of power equipment that integrates
multiple high-voltage components, such as circuit breakers and disconnectors, within a
sealed enclosure, typically using SF or other gases as an insulating media. High-voltage
6
gas-insulated switchgear features a compact structure, small footprint and strong
adaptability to complex environments, and is widely used in scenarios such as urban
power grids and substations to ensure the safe and stable operation of high-voltage systems.
Our high-voltage gas-insulated switchgear primarily includes gas-insulate switchgear (GIS),
gas-insulated transmission lines and hybrid gas-insulated switchgear.
Product Pictures Description
Gas-Insulated Switchgear (GIS)
We provide a range of gas-insulated switchgear (GIS)
products covering voltage levels from 72.5 kV to 1100 kV.
Our gas-insulated switchgear (GIS) products have been
applied in nearly 7,000 projects worldwide.
Gas-Insulated Transmission Line (GIL)
Our gas-insulated transmission line (GIL) products are
designed for voltage levels of 252 kV and 550 kV, featuring
a short-time withstand current of 63 kA. Our gas-insulated
transmission line (GIL) products represent a high-voltage,
large-capacity and reliable transmission solution.
Hybrid Gas-Insulated Switchgear (HGIS)
Hybrid gas-insulated switchgear (HGIS) is an integrated
device that combines modules such as circuit breakers,
three-position switches, current transformers, potential
transformers and fast earthing switches. It features a
compact footprint and strong environmental adaptability.
Hybrid gas-insulated switchgear (HGIS) products cover
voltage levels from 31.5 kV to 252 kV and are suitable for
high-voltage power transmission and distribution
applications, including substations.

Low-Voltage DC Switches
Low-voltage DC switches are specially designed for low-voltage DC circuits. Their
core functions include switching control, overload protection and short-circuit protection,
enabling rapid current interruption in the event of a circuit fault to prevent equipment
damage and ensure safety. We produce a variety of low-voltage DC switches, including DC
frame switch disconnector, DC rotary switch disconnector and DC molded case circuit
breaker and bypass switch, to meet the diverse needs of our customers.
Product Picture Description
DC Frame Switch Disconnector
Our DC frame switch disconnectors are suitable for DC
systems with rated operating voltages of up to 1500 V and a
rated operating current of up to 4000 A. Our DC frame
switch disconnectors provide the functions of connection,
disconnection, isolation and protection for the main circuit.
Our DC frame switch disconnectors are generally used in
DC distribution environments such as energy storage
systems, photovoltaic power generation, electric vehicle
charging facilities and data centers. Our DC frame switch
disconnectors have obtained multiple safety certifications
including CCC, TU¨ V and UL.
DC Rotary Switch Disconnector
Our DC rotary switch disconnectors achieve safe electrical
isolation through a rotary operating mechanism. They are
designed for high-current applications such as DC
distribution systems, energy storage power stations and
rail transit. Our DC rotary switch disconnectors feature
mechanical durability for tens of thousands of operations
and have obtained various safety certifications including
CCC, TU¨ V and UL.
DC Molded Case Circuit Breaker
Our DC molded case circuit breakers have a rated insulation
voltage of 1500 V and a rated operating current range of 100
A to 400 A. They are widely used in photovoltaic power
generation, charging stations, power plants, power supply
systems, rail transit and communications, enabling power
distribution and providing protection for circuits and power
equipment against overloads, short circuits and other faults.
Our DC molded case circuit breakers have obtained CCC
certificate.

Bypass Switch
Our bypass switches are designed for the bypass protection
of voltage source converter sub-modules that adopt a

and becomes unable to operate properly, our bypass
switches can be activated within milliseconds to bypass the
faulty sub-module, thereby ensuring that the overall system

Transformer
Transformers serve as the ‘‘voltage conversion hubs’’ of power transmission and
distribution systems, enabling efficient voltage conversion and energy transfer across
different voltage levels, thereby ensuring both the economic efficiency of power
transmission and the safety of electricity usage. The core products under this business
lines include power transformer, reactor, instrument transformer, bushing, neutral point
grounding product and power capacitor. Our products are widely deployed in major
national infrastructure projects such as the South-to-North Water Diversion Project, the
West-to-East Gas Pipeline Project and the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge, and have
been used in more than 30 countries and regions worldwide.
Power Transformer
A power transformer is a key electrical device that efficiently and safely transfers
electrical energy between different voltage levels, forming a core component of power
transmission and distribution systems. Our power transformer products primarily include
oil-immersed power transformer, gas-insulated power transformer and dry-type
transformer.
Product Picture Description
Oil-Immersed Power Transformer
We supply oil-immersed power transformers with voltage
ratings up to 750 kV. Our oil-immersed power transformers
feature the advantage of in-house R&D and production of
key components. Our oil-immersed power transformers are
characterized by low losses, low noise, low partial discharge
and strong short-circuit withstand capability, making them
suitable for a wide range of installation environments and
operating conditions.

Reactor
A reactor is an electrical device used to control current, limit short-circuit currents and
improve power system stability by providing inductive reactance. Our reactor products
primarily include high-voltage shunt reactor and medium-voltage reactor.
Product Picture Description
High-Voltage Shunt Reactor
Our high-voltage shunt reactors effectively counteract the
capacitive effect of ultra-high-voltage long-distance
transmission lines by absorbing excess reactive power,
thereby improving power transmission efficiency. They
also help suppress harmonic currents in the power system
and enhance the power quality on the user side.

BUSINESS
Product Picture Description
Medium-Voltage Reactor
Our medium-voltage reactor portfolio include both shunt
reactors and series reactors. Shunt reactors are used to
compensate for the capacitive reactance of transmission
lines, making them particularly suitable for lightly loaded
lines to prevent uncontrolled voltage rises. Series reactors
primarily serve to limit the inrush currents during capacitor
switching and to suppress harmonic currents at specific
frequencies. These reactors are featured by low losses, low
temperature rise and low operating noise.
Instrument Transformer
Instrument transformers are essential measurement and protection devices used in
power systems to accurately step down high voltage or high current to lower, standardized
levels for meters, relays and control equipment, while providing electrical isolation between
primary high-voltage circuits and secondary low-voltage systems. By converting real-time
voltage and current signals into manageable values, instrument transformers enable precise
metering, system monitoring and reliable operation of protection schemes, forming a
critical foundation for the safe and stable operation of power grids. Our high-voltage
instrument transformers primarily include voltage transformers, current transformers and
station service voltage transformers.
Product Picture Description
Voltage Transformer
Voltage transformers are used to step down high voltage to
a lower, standardized level for measurement, monitoring
and protection, while providing electrical isolation from
high-voltage circuits. We offer electromagnetic voltage
transformers up to 500 kV, capacitive voltage transformers
up to 1,000 kV and GIS-compatible voltage transformers up
to 1,000 kV. For GIS applications, we have also developed
environmentally friendly products for voltage levels of up to
220 kV.

Product Picture Description
Current Transformer
Current transformers are used to reduce high current to a

devices, ensuring accurate monitoring and safe isolation
between primary and secondary circuits. We provide current

Station Service Voltage Transformer
Station service voltage transformers draw power directly
from high-voltage lines to supply low-voltage electricity for
substation auxiliary systems, remote facilities or temporary
power needs. They typically serve three main functions:
providing power for lighting and protection systems within
switching stations, supplying electrification to remote or
isolated areas and serving as a power source for temporary
or mobile engineering and construction applications.

in power transmission and transformation equipment.
Our bushings portfolio primarily includes transformer bushing, high-current bushing,
oil-gas bushing, GIS outlet bushing, converter transformer valve-side bushing and DC
wall-through bushing.

winding leads out of the tank, providing mechanical
support, insulation and current-carrying capability.

BUSINESS
Neutral Point Grounding Product
Neutral point grounding refers to the method by which the neutral point of power
system equipment, such as generators and transformers, is electrically connected to the
ground through specific devices, including grounding resistors, grounding reactors and
arc-suppression coils. It is a core component of the grounding system of power networks.
Product Picture Description
Grounding Transformer
Grounding transformers are typically used to provide an
artificial neutral point for systems that do not have one,
enabling connection with arc-suppression coils, resistors or
direct grounding.
Arc-suppressing Coil
An arc-suppressing coil provides an inductive current that
compensates for the capacitive fault current during a
ground fault, thereby reducing ground current and
enabling the fault arc to self-extinguish. This effectively
mitigates arc-induced overvoltage.
Grounding Resistor
In distribution networks, grounding the neutral point
through a small resistor is a commonly used grounding
method. This approach effectively limits intermittent
arc-grounding overvoltage and reduces operational
overvoltage in the system.
Flexible Grounding System
A flexible grounding system integrates the advantages of
resonant grounding technology and low-resistance
grounding technology, enabling flexible switching between
grounding modes under various fault conditions in
distribution networks, and reducing feeder trip rates.

power transmission and distribution systems. By providing capacitive reactive power, they
improve power factor, stabilize voltage, reduce line losses and enhance overall grid
efficiency. Power capacitors can also be configured to filter harmonic currents, helping

Static Var Generator/Static Synchronous Compensator
(STATCOM)
A static var generator/static synchronous compensator
(STATCOM) functions as a controllable reactive current
source, capable of providing both capacitive and inductive
reactive power, to rapidly and continuously compensate for
the reactive power demanded by the grid. It improves the
power factor of the supply system and stabilizes system
voltage levels in real time.
Static Synchronous Condenser (E-STATCOM)
Our static synchronous condenser (E-STATCOM)
incorporates advanced grid-forming control technology to
achieve decoupled control of reactive power compensation
and active power support. This enhances voltage regulation
capability while improving system frequency stability,
thereby ensuring the safe and stable operation of new-type
power systems. Our static synchronous condenser
(E-STATCOM) also features an innovative topology and
intelligent operation and maintenance capabilities.
High-Voltage DC Circuit Breakers

‘‘artificial current zero’’ interruption technology. Compared
with hybrid high-voltage DC circuit breakers, our
high-voltage DC circuit breaker features a simple
structure, low conduction losses and cost-effectiveness.
With the steady advancement of new-type power system construction, the importance

Our R&D Teams

Through continuous R&D initiatives, we consistently enhance our technical expertise

process:
Lifecycle
Concept Planning Developmen t Verification Launch
managemen t
. Concept. We conduct market, competitor and historical data analyzes to assess
sales trends and market share. We gather and prioritize requirements, perform
functional analysis and evaluate multiple product and supply-chain concepts to
recommend the optimal solution. We then assess feasibility against defined
requirements and establish the preliminary project management plan.
. Planning. We finalize a full project management plan covering scope, cost,
schedule, quality and risk management. We conduct in-depth risk analysis to
assess the feasibility of targeted market positioning and production capacity,
confirming no material impediments to execution. We design definitive product
and supply chain solutions and formalize all product requirements; develop test,
verification and validation strategies/plans; and complete a detailed financial
assessment of the project.
. Development. We execute detailed product design and establish corresponding
quality control specifications, and design an end-to-end supply chain framework
covering production, procurement and logistics. We manufacture design
prototypes and analyze supply chain processes; plan and implement design
functional verification and product validation activities, conduct internal R&D
testing, and refine the market launch plan in full detail.
. Verification. We implement component-level supply chain processes and conduct
component verification, then roll out product-specific supply chain workflows.
We execute prototype and trial production to validate supply chain processes,
conduct supply chain qualification audits and final product validation activities,
and complete all pre-launch preparations.
. Launch. We verify finished product and mass production stability, conduct
remaining critical tests, track and validate product quality and capacity with
corrective plans as needed, and verify production/logistics performance and
supply chain capabilities. We launch the product commercially, establish an early
warning mechanism for initial customer feedback, and the project team transfers
responsibilities, compiles learnings and assesses commitments to determine
success and post-launch metrics.

Our Core Technologies
We are committed to continuously developing advanced technologies to strengthen our
competitive edge. We have successfully developed several core technologies, including:
Visualization-based Protection and Automation Device Platform
Our visualization-based Protection and Automation Device Platform represents a core
strategic foundation and a key technological roadmap for the future development of power
secondary equipment. Driven by advanced visualization technology, we have built the
industry’s first AC/DC-integrated secondary equipment platform through a highly
integrated, flexible, and open software-hardware architecture, according to Frost &
Sullivan.
Aligned with the international IEC standard, the platform supports comprehensive
graphical and modular visual programming for secondary device development. This enables
developers to perform algorithm design, logic configuration and functional verification in a
more intuitive and efficient manner, significantly reducing development difficulty,
shortening the R&D cycle and greatly improving the flexibility, transparency and
maintainability of protection and control strategies.
This pioneering platform not only achieves deep integration of protection and
automation functions across AC and DC systems, but also offers strong forward
compatibility and scalability. It is designed to meet future diversified application needs
across a wide range of secondary equipment, including substation, distribution, online
monitoring, and power electronics, and is well aligned with international requirements for
enhanced development efficiency, customization capability and lifecycle maintainability in
secondary device engineering.
Grid-forming technology platform
In 2023, we launched our self-developed grid-forming technology platform together
with a suite of serialized grid-forming solutions built on this unified architecture. These
solutions span the full value chain of the conventional power system, including generation,
transmission, transformation and distribution, and extend into power-consumption
scenarios across high-end manufacturing, data centers, transportation hubs, shipping and
logistics, and petroleum refining and chemical industries.
Leveraging our proprietary virtual admittance control algorithms and innovative
dual-star topology, we have developed a series of advanced grid-forming applications such
as ‘‘0 ms’’ fast voltage support, black start capability, inertia support, and short-circuit ratio
enhancement. These applications enhance the secure and stable operation of power systems
ranging from bulk power grids to microgrids, while improving the reliability and continuity
of electricity supply for end-use customers across the entire power system, including the
load side.

BUSINESS
Environmentally friendly gas-insulation technology
Environmentally friendly gas-insulated technology has become a major global trend in
the power equipment industry as an alternative to traditional SF -based insulation, in order
6
to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. We have carried out in-depth research on insulation
technologies for various next-generation eco-friendly gases, including clean air, nitrogen
and carbon dioxide, and have applied these technologies across a full portfolio of
high-voltage power equipment such as gas-insulated switchgear, instrument transformers
and transformers. Compared with traditional SF -insulated equipment, our solutions
6
significantly enhance environmental performance while maintaining essentially the same
insulation reliability and equipment footprint.
Our R&D Testing Capabilities
We established the Electric Testing and Inspection Center (the ‘‘Center’’) in 2011 as our
unified platform for product R&D verification and as a comprehensive testing base. The
Center comprises nine specialized laboratories and has developed multidisciplinary,
end-to-end testing and inspection capabilities that cover the entire power system value
chain. It provides full-process technical support from fundamental research to type testing
and reliability verification.
The Center’s capabilities span multiple professional domains, including power system
analysis and testing, electromagnetic compatibility testing, electrical safety assessment,
environmental and reliability verification, electrical engineering and high-voltage
equipment testing, battery performance and lifetime testing, automotive electronics
testing and power electronics performance evaluation. Equipped with multiple
industry-leading testing platforms and advanced instruments, the Center’s capabilities
extend across high-voltage, strong-current, low-current, power electronics, energy storage,
electrochemistry and automotive electronics technologies, supporting multi-level testing
needs from device-level or module-level to system-level verification.
The Center’s overall performance indicators meet, and in certain areas exceed,
international advanced standards. It is capable of undertaking third-party type testing,
national and industry standard verification, and testing tasks for scientific research
projects. Leveraging this platform, we are able to conduct full-spectrum, full-lifecycle
testing and validation for power equipment, energy-storage products, automotive
electronics and key equipment used in next-generation power systems. This provides
robust technical assurance for new product development, engineering application
verification and quality and reliability improvement, thereby accelerating the
transformation of scientific and technological achievements into engineering applications
and industrialized products.

BUSINESS
Production Process
Our production adheres to the quality standards and product specifications required
by our customers. In order to manufacture high-quality products, we maintain stringent
technical standards in our production processes. The following diagram sets out the main
steps of the production process for our products.
Component and
Incoming material Testing and
Subassembly Final Assembly Deli very
inspection commissioning
Production
. Incoming Material Inspection. We begin our production process with incoming
material inspection. All raw materials, components and purchased parts are
thoroughly checked to ensure they meet our technical specifications and quality
standards. Only qualified materials are released into the production workflow.
. Component and Subassembly Production. After inspection, the materials move into
component and subassembly production. At this stage, key modules and sub-units
are assembled according to standardized procedures, ensuring accuracy,
consistency and readiness for integration into the final product.
. Final Assembly. In the final assembly stage, all pre-assembled modules and
structural parts are integrated into a complete unit. This process focuses on
precise installation, mechanical alignment, electrical connections and overall
structural integrity.
. Testing and Commissioning. Once assembly is complete, each product undergoes
comprehensive testing and commissioning. Depending on the product type, this
may include mechanical, electrical, insulation, sealing, functional or system-level
tests to verify performance, safety and reliability before delivery.
. Delivery. Following successful testing, the product is carefully packaged to
prevent damage during transport. It is then prepared for shipment and delivered
to the customer, completing the production process.
We are committed to the independent R&D and design of core components for
switchgear, as well as the development of assembly capabilities for related production
equipment, ensuring autonomy and controllability in key processes, synchronized
technological iteration, and cost optimization. This enables us to establish a vertically
integrated advantage from core components to complete equipment systems.

MARKETING AND SALES
We sell our products primarily through direct sales. The distribution model is adopted
solely for the overseas sales of energy storage products. We are dedicated to enhancing the
service quality of our sales personnel and distributors to improve customer experience. By
actively managing our sales network, we effectively penetrate global markets and capture
sales opportunities.
Marketing Activities
We are committed to maintaining and enhancing our brand reputation through
marketing activities to showcase our product portfolio. Our marketing and promotion
strategies focus on pre-sales communication with our customers to identify their needs
through methods such as market research and customer visits. We are committed to
providing customized products or solutions based on customer needs.
We actively participate in industry exhibitions, technical conferences and professional
forums/seminars, and use these platforms to present our latest products. In addition, we
work closely with social media platforms and official websites to release information on
technological innovations, product upgrades and application developments, ensuring
continuous exposure and effective communication of our brand information.
In addition, we primarily secure our overseas projects through proactive participation
in direct tenders issued by international project owners, as well as by taking part in projects
undertaken by Chinese and global EPC contractors. These projects are primarily located in
the United Kingdom, Italy, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and other countries and regions.
Leveraging our strong track record and market-leading position in the power transmission
and distribution sector, we are frequently invited by major contractors to participate in
their bidding processes.
Direct Sales
We adopt a direct sales model to reach end customers. We utilize this approach to gain
better understanding of their business needs and deliver customized products and services,
thereby enhancing customer satisfaction and stickiness. During the Track Record Period,
direct sales represented over 99.0% of our sales for each year/period. Our sales and
marketing team possesses extensive professional expertise in our products and effectively
communicates product features and performance to customers. They also play a vital role in
delivering comprehensive customer service.
The typical salient terms of the sales agreements with our direct sales customers during
the Track Record Period are set out below:
Product specification. The agreement specifies product types, specifications, prices,
quantities and other detailed terms, which are ultimately confirmed in the individual
purchase orders we issue to our suppliers.

Distributorship
We maintain a distributor network for our overseas energy storage systems and
components, enabling us to efficiently reach and support global customers with our service,
enhancing our market expansion capabilities. Our distributors are also our customers, and
we maintain buyer-seller relationships with them. In 2023, 2024 and the nine months ended
September 30, 2025, we conducted transactions with 19, 48 and 42 distributors, respectively.
During the Track Record Period, revenue from sales to our distributors represented less
than 1.0% of our sales for each year/period.
We prioritize distributors with proven track records, strong operational credentials
and a high level of market recognition and influence. We manage distributors across
multiple dimensions, including marketing, after-sales service and compliance with policies
and regulations, by establishing core indicators for distributor management and operations.
Our sales personnel visit distributors to provide support, assess sales performance and
understand business needs. We believe that our sales through distributorship reflect actual
demand from our end customers, thereby minimizing the risk of channel stuffing and
inventory backlog within the distribution network, because we generally do not allow
product returns from distributors, except for limited circumstances such as product defects.
We typically enter into standard distribution agreements with our distributors. The
following sets forth a summary of the key commercial terms and arrangements that we
typically enter into with our distributors:
Terms. The term of the distribution agreements is generally two years.
Scope of Authorization. The distributor is only authorized to distribute the relevant
products within a specified territory.
Sub-Distributor. The distributor may appoint sub-distributors to act on its behalf, and
any compensation payable to such sub-distributors shall be the sole responsibility of the
distributor.

OUR SERVICES
We are committed to becoming a global leader in the electrical industry, and service is
important for us to strategically transform from an equipment manufacturer to an
integrated solutions provider.
In 2023, we established our Global Engineering Service Center to operate a
platform-based service system, providing full-lifecycle technical services to our global
customers. As of September 30, 2025, we had a professional service team of over 1,000
members and more than 40 service locations worldwide. To enhance responsiveness, we
have deployed spare-parts warehouses at these locations to support emergency material
supply. Through a ‘‘local teams + localized warehousing’’ model, we ensure rapid resource
allocation and efficient fault handling, enabling real-time response to customer needs, swift
issue resolution and reliable product operation.
The Global Engineering Service Center’s scope of services is primarily divided into
three categories: commissioning services, O&M support and life-extension services.
. Commissioning services refer to the comprehensive after-sales services provided
before the product is put into operation. These services cover on-site equipment
positioning and installation after delivery; system-level and component-level
commissioning; technical guidance and support during installation; functional
commissioning and parameter optimization; and handover tests, including
insulation tests, protection verification, functional verification and other key
procedures.

. O&M support refers to the comprehensive services carried out throughout the

our service system and integrating digitalization capabilities, we have enhanced the
economic benefits delivered by products to customers.
After-Sales and Warranty
We have developed a standard product return procedure. When a customer requests
the return of non-conforming products, the customer needs to provide us with
non-conforming samples and we shall accept the return request upon determination of
any non-conformity. During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable
Date, we had not experienced any material product return or recall due to defects in our
products.
In our ongoing efforts to maintain customer satisfaction and improve our products and
services, our after-sales team is responsible for providing comprehensive after-sales services.
They can diagnose issues and identify products for customers’ problems. For significant
customer complaints that involve production halts, claims or recalls, quality engineers are
required to compile relevant information in writing and report to expedite resolution. We
provide after-sales services such as repair, replacement and returns for our customers based
on the specific circumstances of the product in accordance with the applicable laws and
regulations. We have established after-sales service and warranty management procedures.
When on-site warranty service is required, our after-sales personnel will bring the necessary
repair equipment to provide service on-site. All after-sales personnel providing on-site
after-sales service have undergone rigorous trainings and are only permitted to attend to
customer sites after they have passed assessments.

BUSINESS
Supplier Selection and Management
When selecting suppliers, we take into account a number of factors, including the
supplier’s duration of operation, compliance with onboarding standards, validity of
qualification certificates and integrity in business operations. We have implemented a
systematic supplier management system that governs the onboarding of suppliers,
management of qualified suppliers and termination of unqualified suppliers to ensure the
efficiency of our supplier management processes. We carry out performance assessments of
our suppliers on a regular basis to ensure the quality of their products and services, and
inform them of our assessment results and rectification requirements.
We generally procure raw materials from suppliers through non-exclusive supply
contracts. To ensure stable raw material supply, we adopt proactive supplier management
policies, including maintaining more qualified suppliers for key materials and identifying
alternative suppliers. As of September 30, 2025, we collaborated with more than 1,500
suppliers worldwide. We have established long-term relationships with suppliers that
provide sufficient raw material availability and reliable supply channels. For critical raw
materials and components, we typically enter into framework supply agreements with
suppliers, the key terms of which are summarized below.
Duration. The framework supply agreement terms are generally one year.
Product specification. The framework supply agreement may specify product types,
specifications, prices, quantities, delivery timelines and other detailed terms, which are
ultimately confirmed in the individual purchase orders we issue to our suppliers.
Delivery. The suppliers are responsible for delivery of raw materials and/or
components to our designated location specified in each purchase order.
Quality control. We usually inspect and accept products in accordance with our
specifications, as well as national, local and industry standards, and the requirements of
quality agreements. Should any quality issues arise during the warranty period, the supplier
shall be responsible for replacement.
Payment. We are responsible for making the payments to the suppliers and the
suppliers shall provide us with the corresponding invoice.
During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, we did not
experience any material breach of the agreements with our suppliers.

INVENTORY AND LOGISTICS MANAGEMENT
We have established a comprehensive inventory and logistics management system
underpinned by standardized operational processes and full-process digitalized
management capabilities to streamline the operational workflow, enhance operational
efficiency and mitigate potential operational and supply chain risks.
Inventory Management
Our inventories consist of raw materials, work in progress, finished goods and goods in
transit. As of December 31, 2023, 2024 and September 30, 2025, our inventories were
RMB2,860.8 million, RMB3,477.0 million and RMB5,027.0 million, respectively. For the
years ended December 31, 2023, 2024 and the nine months ended September 30, 2025, our
inventory turnover days were 109 days, 108 days and 124 days, respectively. We actively
manage our inventory by adjusting our production, sales and inventory plans. This process
is based on market demand forecasts and factors such as price fluctuations of raw materials
and components. Through our sales and operations planning system and taking into
consideration the procurement cycle, we place orders for raw materials and components,
maintaining sufficient supply of raw materials.
Logistics
Our products are typically delivered directly from our warehouses to the venue
specified by our customers, with the shipping costs generally borne by us. We engage
qualified third-party logistics service providers for delivery to our customers in compliance
with product specifications. Our contracts with third-party logistics service providers

QUALITY CONTROL
We attach paramount importance to product quality control, as we believe that
stringent quality governance is a cornerstone for building and elevating our brand
reputation and fostering long-term trust among our customers. We have established and
fully implemented a robust, standardized quality control management system that aligns
with authoritative national and international quality standards. This quality control
management system covers the entire value chain, spanning every critical link from raw
material sourcing, supplier screening and supply chain management to the entire product
manufacturing process. We strictly enforce rigorous product safety and quality control
criteria, and deploy systematic, multi-dimensional quality control measures across the
entire production lifecycle from initial production preparation to final finished product
delivery.
We have obtained a comprehensive portfolio of authoritative qualification
certifications, including ISO 9001, ISO14001, ISO45001 and IATF16949. Our quality
control measures include standardized quality management system operation, product
design quality assurance and verification, incoming raw material and component quality
inspection, in-process real-time quality control and process validation, final assembly
performance testing, finished product comprehensive quality inspection, ex-factory delivery
quality confirmation, end-to-end supplier quality management and supply chain quality
control.

TRANSFER PRICING ARRANGEMENT
Our Company, our controlled affiliates and subsidiaries carry out intra-group
transactions in accordance with market prices and our Group’s transfer pricing policy.
Such policy adheres to the arm’s-length principle. During the Track Record Period and up
to the Latest Practicable Date, our Company, our controlled affiliates and subsidiaries had
been engaged in certain intra-group transactions involving the buy-sell transactions of
products. We (acting as principal) sell products to our Group’s overseas distribution
entities, which then further sell the products to third-party customers.
The Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (‘‘OECD’’), an
international organization fostering cross-border cooperation, issued the Transfer Pricing
Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises and Tax Administrations (the ‘‘OECD Transfer
Pricing Guidelines’’). These guidelines are widely adopted by tax authorities worldwide in
evaluating related-party transactions. In accordance with the OECD Transfer Pricing
Guidelines, transactions within our Group’s entities should be carried out in commensurate
with the arm’s length principle.
We have appointed an international professional accounting firm as our transfer
pricing advisor (the ‘‘Transfer Pricing Advisor’’) to review our transfer pricing
arrangements. The Transfer Pricing Advisor has reviewed the related-party transactions
under concern (‘‘Covered Transactions’’) to determine whether the profit levels achieved by
our subsidiaries involved in these transactions have achieved an arm’s-length level of
profits. This analysis was conducted in accordance with the OECD Transfer Pricing
Guidelines released in 2022. The transfer pricing regulations in PRC and other relevant tax
jurisdictions are consistent with the approach outlined in the OECD Transfer Pricing
Guidelines.
Based on the Transfer Pricing Advisor’s assessment of the Covered Transactions and
the transfer pricing benchmarking analysis, which involved screening and evaluating
comparable companies, the net profit margin or gross profit margin levels of the relevant
entities are reasonable and commensurate with their respective functions and risks.
Therefore, the profit levels of the reviewed entities comply with the arm’s length principle.
During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, we were not
aware of any outstanding enquiries, audit, investigation or challenge by any tax authorities
in the PRC and other relevant tax jurisdictions in relation to our intra-group transactions
and transfer pricing arrangements.

INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY

enhancing efficiency, transparency and overall management quality.

for system access and usage.
